legend.title: What the statuses mean
legend.intro: The same colours mean the same thing everywhere: green is fine, amber needs attention, red is broken, grey is unknown.
legend.history: History: how did a sync end?
legend.actions: Plan actions: what a sync will do

Synced.label: Synced
Synced.description: Discord matches the active revision in git.

OutOfSync.label: Out of sync
OutOfSync.description: Discord differs from the active revision. The next sync applies the plan.

Unknown.label: Unknown
Unknown.description: Not compared yet: no bot connected or no sync so far.

Progressing.label: Progressing
Progressing.description: Starting or syncing; it should settle shortly.

Degraded.label: Degraded
Degraded.description: The last operation failed. The message explains why and how to fix it.

Missing.label: Missing
Missing.description: Not running: the bot is not connected or the server is not reachable.

failed.label: Failed
failed.description: Discord refused one or more changes. Nothing else was rolled back.

rejected.label: Rejected
rejected.description: The revision is invalid; the runtime kept the last valid one.

create.label: Create
create.description: Declared in YAML, missing on Discord: it will be created.

update.label: Update
update.description: Exists on Discord with different values: they will be changed.

delete.label: Delete
delete.description: Removed from YAML and pruning is on: it will be deleted on Discord.

adopt.label: Adopt
adopt.description: An existing resource with the same name becomes managed by CODI.

reorder.label: Reorder
reorder.description: Positions will be changed to follow the YAML order.

unmanage.label: Unmanage
unmanage.description: Removed from YAML: CODI stops managing it but leaves it on Discord.

blocked.label: Blocked
blocked.description: A safety rule prevents this change; it is not applied.

errors.otherFailures_one: {{count}} other change failed in the same sync.
errors.otherFailures_other: {{count}} other changes failed in the same sync.

network.title: Can't reach the runtime
network.message: The CODI runtime did not answer.
network.hint: Check that codi is running and reachable, then retry.

forbidden.message: Your role on this server does not allow this.

notFound.title: Not found
notFound.message: It may have been removed from the repository.

conflict.title: Changed since you opened it
conflict.message: Someone changed the configuration in the meantime.
conflict.hint: Reload to get the latest version, then redo your change.

invalid.title: Some values are invalid
invalid.hint: Fix the highlighted fields and try again.

unavailable.title: The runtime is not ready
unavailable.message: The runtime cannot do this right now.
unavailable.hint: Check the bot status, then retry in a moment.

internal.title: The runtime hit an internal error
internal.message: This is a bug in CODI, not in your configuration.
internal.hint: Retry; if it persists, check the runtime logs.

boost.description: Live from Discord. Some settings need a boost level: the plan blocks them with a reason until the server reaches it.

community.short: Unlocks announcement and stage channels, the rules and updates channels, the welcome screen, native onboarding, discovery and insights.

unlocks.channels: Rules, community updates and safety alerts channels

community.howTo: Enable it in the YAML with community.enabled: true. Discord requires a rules channel and an updates channel, verification level low or higher and the explicit content filter on all members.

setup.title: Set up CODI
setup.simulatorHint: This runtime uses the Discord simulator: the buttons marked “Simulate” stand in for what you would do on discord.com.

access.title: Open the setup link
access.text: For security, the setup wizard only opens with the one-time link CODI printed in its logs when it started. It looks like {{example}}.
access.placeholder: Paste the link from the logs
access.restart: Each link works once. Lost it? Restart CODI: it prints a new one.

completed.title: CODI is already set up
completed.text: The setup wizard has been completed. Sign in to the admin console to manage your server.

welcome.title: Let's get your Discord server running on CODI
welcome.lead: In about ten minutes, CODI will manage your server's roles, channels and permissions, and run plugins like welcome messages or tickets. Every change is saved as a version you can review or undo.

items.bot: You create a Discord bot and paste its token: CODI checks it and finds everything else itself.
items.invite: You add the bot to your server with one link. CODI checks it has the rights it needs.
items.import: CODI reads your server as it is today and saves it. Nothing on Discord changes.
items.verify: CODI verifies everything live, then you can add a first plugin.

welcome.question: Where are you starting from?
welcome.existing: I already have a Discord server
welcome.existingText: CODI adopts your roles and channels as they are.
welcome.newText: Create an empty server first, CODI takes it from there.
welcome.newSteps: In Discord, click the “+” at the bottom of your server list → “Create My Own” → give it a name. Come back here once it exists.

discord.title: Create your bot
discord.lead: A bot is how CODI acts on your server. You create it once in Discord's Developer Portal; it takes two minutes.
discord.step1: Open the Developer Portal and click “New Application”. The name you choose is your bot's name (you can change it later). Accept the terms and click “Create”.
discord.step2: In the left menu, open “Bot”, click “Reset Token”, confirm, then click “Copy”. Discord shows the token only once.
discord.step3: Paste the token below. CODI checks it with Discord and stores it encrypted; it is never shown again.
discord.tokenPlaceholder: Paste the token copied from the Bot page
discord.tokenHelp: It is a long text with two dots. Not the Application ID, not the Client Secret.
discord.simCreated: A simulated bot was created and its token pasted below.
discord.intentsLead: Some plugins need to see who joins the server or what messages say. Discord asks you to turn these on explicitly.
discord.intentToggles: On the Bot page, scroll to “Privileged Gateway Intents” and turn on:

server.title: Add the bot to your server
server.lead: Open the invite link, choose your server and click “Authorize”. Keep “Administrator” checked: CODI manages roles, channels and permissions for you.
server.inviteDetails: Asks for the “bot” and “applications.commands” scopes with the Administrator permission.
server.simLow: Place the bot's role at the bottom (to try the fix)
server.watching: Watching for new servers… it appears here a few seconds after you click Authorize.
server.none: The bot is not in any server yet.
server.noManage: You need the “Manage Server” permission on a server to add a bot to it. Usually the server owner does it.
server.simRaise: Simulate: drag the bot role to the top

repo.title: Where should CODI keep your configuration?
repo.lead: CODI saves your server's setup as files. Every change made in the admin is a new version, so you can see what changed and go back.

providers.embeddedText: Stored by CODI next to its data, with full history. No git or GitHub account needed.
providers.githubText: For teams who review changes on GitHub. CODI pushes the first version for you.
providers.localText: Development: the files are written to the folder “codi dev” watches; edit them in your editor.

repo.urlHelp: Create an empty repository on GitHub first (it can be private).
repo.tokenHelp: Create a fine-grained token with “Contents: Read and write” on this repository. It is stored encrypted.
repo.importLead: CODI reads {{name}} as it is today (roles, channels, permissions) and saves it as the first version. Nothing changes on Discord.
repo.activated: Your server is now managed by CODI
repo.proof: Proof: CODI compared the saved configuration with Discord and found nothing to change.
repo.proofChanges_one: CODI found {{count}} difference between the configuration and Discord.
repo.proofChanges_other: CODI found {{count}} differences between the configuration and Discord.
repo.needsConfirm: Applying this configuration would change Discord
repo.needsConfirmText: Usually the import adopts everything as it is. Review these changes before applying them.

login.title: Sign in to the admin with Discord
login.lead: Optional but recommended: lets you (and your moderators) sign in to this admin console with Discord. Server owners are admins automatically.
login.step1: Open the OAuth2 page of your application.
login.step2: Under “Redirects”, click “Add Redirect”, paste this URL, then “Save Changes”:
login.step3: Click “Reset Secret”, copy the Client Secret and paste it below.
login.fromEnv: The client secret comes from the CODI_DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET environment variable.
login.testing: Waiting for the login in the other tab…
login.returnText: You can close this tab and go back to the setup wizard.
login.simText: With the simulator, you sign in with “dev login” (any simulated user): nothing to configure here.
login.skipWarning: Without it, only the setup link can open the admin. You can configure it later (CODI_DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET).

verify.title: Let's check everything works
verify.lead: CODI runs these checks live. Fix anything red, then they update on their own.
verify.sendMessage: Send a message in any channel of {{name}} (for example “hello CODI”). This proves CODI receives events from Discord.

plugin.title: Add your first plugin
plugin.lead: Plugins are the features of your bot. Pick one to try; you can add more later from the admin.
plugin.tryIt: Try it now: type /{{command}} in a channel of {{server}}.
plugin.noCommand: It reacts to what happens on your server.
plugin.pr: A pull request was opened: the plugin is active once it is merged.

done.title: You're all set
done.adminText: Roles, channels, plugins, history and diagnostics.
done.loginWarning: Admin login is not configured: once you finish, the setup link stops working. Configure Discord login first, or set CODI_DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET later.

install.botHint: Several bots manage this server: pick the one that runs the plugin.
install.instanceHint: Unique on the bot. Several instances of a plugin can run side by side.
install.intentsWarning: Needs {{intents}} enabled in the Discord developer portal, otherwise the install is refused.
install.confirm: I trust {{publisher}}, the publisher of {{name}} from the unofficial source {{source}}, and grant it:

confirmation.title: Confirmation required

intents.title: A privileged intent is off

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Where CODI looks for plugins. The built-in codi source is always there; registries are declared in codi.yaml (spec.registries).
sources.name: Name
sources.cannotRemove: The built-in codi source cannot be removed

add.title: Add a registry
add.text: A registry is a git repository with an index.yaml listing plugins.
add.risk: Registries you add are unofficial: CODI does not review their plugins. Add only sources you trust; installing their plugins is at your own risk.
add.name: Name
add.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, up to 32 characters.

errors.namePattern: Start with a letter or digit; use only a-z, 0-9 and -, up to 32 characters
errors.nameReserved: codi is reserved for the built-in source
errors.nameTaken: A source with this name already exists

confirmRemove.title: Remove the source {{name}}?
confirmRemove.text: Its plugins can no longer be installed. This changes codi.yaml for the whole project. Instances already using the source block the removal.

forbidden.title: You cannot change the sources
forbidden.text: Sources live in codi.yaml and apply to the whole project: adding or removing one needs the admin role on every server CODI manages.

result.prText: The change applies once the pull request is merged.
